transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

Warm or even quite hot sides aren't normally a fire risk, because many fridge freezers deliberately release heat through pipes built into the side panels, but in a tight alcove that heat can't escape well, so the fridge works harder. If you ever notice a burning smell, scorch marks or sides too hot to keep your hand on, switch it off at the wall and stop using it. From what you have described, the most likely cause is dusty coils or too little space round it. Fridge freezers lose their heat through a coil or grille at the back or underneath. Gently dust or vacuum it, and leave a few centimetres of space between it and the wall or cupboards. Was it dusty or pushed against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space round it?

It's only 2 months old so shouldn't be dusty, and there are no visible coils on the back anyway. It's in a tight alcove though, about 1cm each side and a few cm gap to the cupboard above. I can keep my hand on the sides, no burning smell, and it's cooling well.
Is the freezer still cold while the fridge is warm, and is there a thick block of ice on the back wall inside the freezer?
Fridge and freezer temperatures are 4C and -18C, so both are cold. I haven't noticed any ice build-up, but I'm not sure I'd know what to look for. It's just the outside that's warm.

This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: A new or moved fridge-freezer should stand upright for several hours before switching on (check the manual) and takes up to 24 hours to reach temperature. It would be worth a closer look if still not cold after 24 hours. Behind the rear panel inside the freezer, are the coils a solid block of ice, or fairly clear?
I haven't looked behind the rear panel inside the freezer, and I'm not sure how to tell. Everything inside is cold though. Is the warmth on the outside sides normal for this sort of fridge?

Some warmth on the sides is normal for a fridge-freezer with no visible coils on the back, because these models usually release their heat through pipes inside the side panels, and the front edges often feel warm too. Whether this much warmth is normal depends on what is driving it, which isn't clear from the outside alone, so it's worth ruling out a fault rather than assuming it's fine. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the automatic defrost system. The first step is a full manual defrost: switch it off at the socket, move the food into cool bags, put towels down and leave the doors open until every bit of ice has melted, then dry it and switch it back on. Have you been able to do a full defrost, or is there no ice to clear?
I haven't done a defrost, and I'm not sure there's any ice to clear. Everything inside is cold and working fine, so is a full defrost really necessary? I'd rather not do it unless it's needed.

Probably not. A full defrost is usually only needed if there's thick ice that never clears or the drain hole is frozen solid, and you haven't noticed any build-up. This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: In most fridges the back wall frosts while the compressor runs and then melts and runs into the drain channel when it stops: a thin layer of frost or droplets that comes and goes is normal. Frost-free freezers defrost automatically every few hours and may hiss or drip during that time. It would be worth a closer look if thick ice that never clears, water pooling on the shelves or floor, or the fridge getting warm. Ice in the bottom often means the defrost water can't drain away. At the bottom of the back wall there's a small drain hole — once the ice has melted, clear it gently with warm water or a soft pipe cleaner. Was the drain hole blocked (and is it clear now), is it still blocked or frozen, or was it already clear?

I haven't checked the drain hole and haven't seen any water or ice, so I don't think it's blocked. Can you tell me whether the warm sides are normal for this model, given the tight alcove? I'd rather not pull it out because of our new floor.

Yes, warm sides are normal for many fridge-freezers like yours with no visible coils on the back, because the condenser pipes that give off heat run inside the side panels, and yours is still cooling properly. Whether a 1cm gap is enough depends on the minimum clearances in your model's installation guide, since a tight alcove can make the sides feel warmer than they would with more space around This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: The sides or front between the doors of many fridge-freezers get warm: the condenser and anti-condensation pipes run there. Normal. It would be worth a closer look if the outside is hot to touch with the inside not cooling, or a burning smell. Run your fingers round the rubber seal on the door and look for splits, gaps or a section that has come away, especially where the frost is. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

I haven't checked the door seal, and I'm not sure what a faulty one would look like. The doors seem to close fine and everything inside is cold. The manual does say to leave some space round it, but I haven't checked the exact clearances. Does 1cm each side sound enough to you?

It depends on the figure your manual gives, since the manual says to leave space, but 1cm is on the tight side. On fridge-freezers with no coils on the back, the sides release the heat, so a tight gap mainly makes the sides feel warmer and the fridge work a little harder rather than causing a fault. Then no repair is needed. If it ever does it in a way that does not fit that, get back in touch and we will look further.
